findings.title: Prevent concurrent builds for the same namespaced key
findings.body: Holding cacheMu only for publication allows GetIndex to return nil while another build for that key is in progress. getOrCreateIndex has no per-key synchronization, so a search request and the write-event consumer can build separate indexes for the same namespace/resource. The consumer can publish and update one index, then a slower build can overwrite the cache with an older snapshot, losing that update from subsequent searches. Disk-backed builds can also concurrently call bleve.New for the same directory. Add per-key synchronization or singleflight while retaining parallel builds for different keys.

findings.title: Protect TotalDocs from concurrent cache insertion
findings.body: This new TotalDocs call runs after the search write-event goroutine has started. The Bleve implementation of TotalDocs iterates b.cache without taking cacheMu.RLock. A write event for a namespace omitted from initial indexing can concurrently call BuildIndex and insert into that map, causing a data race and potentially a fatal concurrent-map-iteration/write error during startup. Synchronize TotalDocs with cache writes, or obtain the count before starting the consumer.

findings.title: Handle closed event channels before eagerly starting consumers
findings.body: Eager Init now starts the search event consumer during construction, even when no storage RPC is ever made. With the SQL backend also supplied as Lifecycle, server.Stop calls backend.Stop, and the SQL poller closes its event stream. The consumer in search.init receives from that channel without checking whether it is closed and calls handleEvent with nil, which dereferences evt.Type and panics. Thus constructing and stopping a search-enabled server without making any RPC now exercises a crashing lifecycle that previously started no consumer. Make the event loop exit on channel closure or cancellation.

findings.title: Retain stopped-state rejection in request handlers
findings.body: Removing Init from the request handlers also removes their stopped-state check. Stop records "service is stopping" or "service is stopped" in initErr, which the old handler calls to Init returned to callers. Eager constructor initialization does not replace that check after shutdown begins. For example, SQL backend.Stop only stops polling and leaves the database usable, so authenticated Create/Update/Delete calls can still commit after the resource server is stopped, without functioning watch/index maintenance. Retain a lifecycle-state guard independently of initialization.
